mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 5-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rates and declining labor market slack (measured by UNRATE) signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that simultaneously increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2pp in 1 month AND UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS rise > 0.2pp and UNRATE fall > 0.1pp) fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of instances over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a high labor market tightness regime (measured by UNRATE below 4.0%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as companies face rising wage pressures that erode profit margins, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC between HOUST and 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1250.0 thousand units for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening in the housing market and reduced consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1250.0 for 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > 5.0% in 1 month AND INDPRO falls > 1.0% in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST fall > 5.0% and INDPRO fall > 1.0%) fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of instances over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply recovery regime (measured by INDPRO above 105.0), the S&P 500 tends to outperform as manufacturing output expands, boosting corporate profits and leading to positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO > 105.0.
